Pyka and Grupo HAME Begin Guatemala’s First Autonomous Electric Aerial Crop Spraying Operation

In classic startup-fashion, Pyka was started in Michael's parents' garage. The garage was not large enough to fit Pyka's proof of concept vehicle, "Big Bird," so the company moved to the backyard, where they maintained a decidedly laid back 'shoes optional' corporate culture.
After raising a $3m round out of Y Combinator, the team set about designing and building its first product, the "Egret," which was a 200lb payload 100% autonomous electric crop duster.

Four months after raising their Seed+, Pyka flew its second generation electric autonomous ag airplane, the "Pelican". The new aircraft incorporated dozens of design and feature improvements and carried over 3x the liquid payload of its predecessor.
Pelican Enters Production

Pyka started serial production of the Pelican in late 2020, after completing structural load testing and flight testing programs. Most of the aircraft is manufactured at our facility in Oakland, California.
April 2021
Pelican SN3 was delivered to one of two major launch customers in Costa Rica where the aircraft would soon go to work spraying Bananas.
The Pelican successfully completed the final stage of flight demonstration for commercial approval in the US.
April 2022
Pyka secured the world's first approval for autonomous night spray operations in Costa Rica.
April 2023
Pyka secured FAA 44807 Authorization for Commercial Operation of Pelican Spray in the United States.

Crop spraying by manned aircraft is one of the more dangerous jobs in agriculture, flying low and fast over fields, and it is expensive to staff. At the same time, moving cargo, whether pesticide, food, or military supplies, to remote or damaged locations often depends on infrastructure like runways, fuel and trained crew that are not always available where the cargo is needed.

Both problems share a common shape: a flight that is repetitive, risky for a human pilot, or logistically constrained by needing a person and full-size airport infrastructure on board or on the ground.

Pyka's aircraft are built to remove the pilot from that equation entirely, flying spraying missions over farmland or long cargo routes autonomously, using aircraft the company designs and builds itself rather than retrofitting existing manned aircraft.
An autonomous electric aircraft that sprays crops, with a stated 300-litre payload and an operating cost the company puts at about US$1 per hectare.
Pyka’s goal is to provide society with a new form of safe, clean, and cost-effective transportation enabled by autonomous electric aviation.

We design, develop and manufacture an ecosystem of technologies including proprietary flight control software, avionics, high power density motors, motor controllers, batteries, and custom carbon-fiber composite airframes.

Today, we supply autonomous electric aircraft for cargo transport and crop protection to real-world customers across four separate continents and have secured industry-first regulatory approvals from the FAA.
